introduction: On this Sunday, seven brothers and their mother face death rather than betray God's law, confident that God will raise them up. In the Gospel, the Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, try to trap Jesus, and he answers that God is the God not of the dead but of the living, for all are alive to him. Paul prays that the Lord may strengthen our hearts. Let us live in the hope of the resurrection.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God is the God of the living. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may bear joyful witness to the hope of the resurrection. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are persecuted for their faith: that they may be strengthened, like the seven brothers and their mother. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who doubt life after death: that they may come to know the God of the living. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the dying and for those who mourn: that the hope of the resurrection may give them peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that the Lord may direct our hearts to the love of God and the endurance of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of the living, all are alive to you. Strengthen our hope in the resurrection, keep us faithful in every trial, and bring us to eternal life. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The God of the living
reflection.body:
The Second Book of Maccabees tells of a mother and her seven sons who are tortured to force them to break God's law. They refuse. One of them says, "we are ready to die rather than transgress the laws of our ancestors." Their courage comes from hope: "the King of the world will raise us who have died for his laws up to an everlasting renewal of life." Another says, "It is good to die at the hands of men and look for the hope which is given by God, that we will be raised up again by him."

In the Gospel, the Sadducees, who do not believe in the resurrection, bring Jesus a question meant to make the idea look ridiculous. A woman marries seven brothers in turn, each one dying childless. "Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them will she be?"

Jesus answers that the life of the resurrection is not simply a continuation of this life. Those who rise "neither marry nor are given in marriage. For they can't die any more, for they are like the angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection." Then he points to Moses at the burning bush, where God calls himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, long after their deaths. "Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for all are alive to him."

God's relationship with those he loves is not broken by death. Our loved ones who have died in Christ are alive to God.

Paul prays for the Thessalonians, and for us: "May the Lord direct your hearts into God's love and into the perseverance of Christ." And he assures them, "But the Lord is faithful, who will establish you and guard you from the evil one."

This week, pray for someone you have lost, trusting that they are alive to God. And ask for the courage to remain faithful, whatever it costs.
